# Salt River at McDowell, Ariz. a

Location. - Lat. 33°33' long. 111°39' in NE1 sec. 5, T. 2 N., R. 7 E., unsurveyed, 1.7 miles or less upstream from Verde River and 61 miles south of McDovell (also called Fort McDowell).

chunks.content:
# Salt River at McDowell, Ariz. a (cont.)

Average discharge. 9 years (water years, 1898-99, 1904-10), 1,562 second-feet.

Extremes.- 1895-1910: Maximum daily discharge, 138,000 second-feet Nov. 27, 1905 (gage height, 21.2 feet), from rating curve extended above 60,000 second-feet; minimum daily, 38 second-feet July 14, 16, 1904.

Gage. - 1907-10: Records were furnished, and no details regarding gagns are available; however, all gages were within less than 1.7 miles upstream from Vorde River. Usual methods of stream gaging were employed for 1907-9 and probably for 1910. 1895-96: Records were furnished, and no details regarding gager are available. Discharge measurements were made about a mile upstream from Verde River by the float- area method for high stages and perhaps for all stages.

# Salt River at McDowell, Ariz. a (cont.)

From 1897 to 1907 vertical staff gages were used as follows: Apr. 20, 1897, to Nov. 30, 1899, on left bank 0.6 mile upstream from Verde River; Jan. 1, 1901, to Apr. 2, 1903, on right bank 1.1 mile upstream from Verde River: Ma 19, 1903, to Mar. 9, 1905, and Mar. 20 to Apr. 14, 1905, on left bank 1.7 miles upstream from Verde River; Mar. 10-19, 1905, on right bank 1.4 miles upstream from Verde River; Apr. 15, 1905, to 1907 and probably longer, on right bank 0.7 mile upstream from Verde River. Gages were read to hundredths or half-tenths twice daily. Datum 04 gage used begin- ning Jan. 1, 1901, was 1,323.59 feet above mean sea level; datum o.4 gage used begin- ning May 19, 1903, was 1,336.27 feet above mean sea level; datum of gage used begin- ning Apr. 15, 1905, was 1.330.62 feet above mean sea level until Sept. 1, 1905, when it was lowered 4 feet. Datum above mean sea level referred to is Geological Survey datum at that time.

chunks.content:
# Salt River at McDowell, Ariz. a (cont.)

Cooperation. - Records for 1895-96 furnished by Hudson Reservoir and Canal Company and those for 1907-10 furnished by Bureau of Reclamation.

Remarks. - Records for 1897-1902 probably fair and for 1903-6 good except those above 10,000 second-feet, which are poor. The period 1903-6 is rated good because of the very large number of discharge measurements which were made, well distributed accord- ing to stage of the river and time. Diversions above station for irrigation. No regulation prior to construction of Roosevelt Dam; the first regulation definitely caused by Roosevelt Dam was in November 1908 but some small effect probably occurred earlier. Full-scale storage behind Roosevelt Dam began in 1910.

Monthly summary of discharge of Salt River at MoDowell, Ariz., 1875-99, 1901-10

(t Partly estimated; I Corrected)
